skill.name: golang-performance
skill.description: Go performance optimization guidance for profiled bottlenecks, code review, benchmarks, memory allocation, CPU hot paths, runtime tuning, caching, and production observability.
skill.summary: Diagnose and optimize Go performance bottlenecks with profiling-based patterns.
skill.author: samber

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code spans, Go examples, evaluation prompts, local profiling URLs, and temporary benchmark filenames. I found no prompt-injection attempt, hidden execution path, credential access, data exfiltration, or malicious intent in the reviewed skill files.

remediation.issue: Command examples and temporary file paths trigger automated scanners.
remediation.suggestion: Keep commands clearly fenced as examples and state that users should run profiling commands only on trusted local projects.

remediation.issue: Evaluation fixtures contain many prompt snippets that resemble executable content.
remediation.suggestion: Consider labeling evals/evals.json as non-executable test data in repository documentation to reduce reviewer ambiguity.

content.value_statement: Go services often slow down because teams optimize before proving the real bottleneck. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through profiling-based fixes for CPU, memory, I/O, caching, and runtime issues.
actual_capabilities: Maps profiled bottleneck signals to concrete Go optimization patterns.
Reviews Go hot paths for allocation, CPU, I/O, caching, and runtime issues.
Recommends benchmark and benchstat workflows to compare changes.
Explains memory layout, sync.Pool, GC, GOMAXPROCS, and PGO tradeoffs.
Provides production observability guidance for Prometheus, pprof, and continuous profiling.
Connects related Go skill references for benchmarking, concurrency, database, and observability topics.
limitations: It assumes profiling or benchmark data is available before optimization begins.
It does not replace a full benchmarking methodology skill.
It can suggest third-party tools, but users must verify current APIs and licenses.
Some runtime guidance depends on the Go version and deployment environment.

best_practices: Collect a baseline profile or benchmark before changing code.
Apply one optimization at a time and compare results with benchstat or production metrics.
Document benchmark evidence next to non-obvious optimizations.
anti_patterns: Do not optimize based only on intuition or isolated code style preferences.
Do not use unsafe or experimental runtime features without benchmark proof and rollback options.
Do not hide I/O, database, or upstream latency behind CPU micro-optimizations.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it after profiling, benchmarking, or code review identifies a Go performance bottleneck.

faq.question: Does it write benchmarks for me?
faq.answer: It can suggest benchmark checks, but it points detailed benchmark workflow to a dedicated benchmarking skill.

faq.question: Can it help with memory problems?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers allocation reduction, backing array leaks, sync.Pool, struct layout, GC pressure, and memory limits.

faq.question: Can it help with CPU profiles?
faq.answer: Yes. It maps CPU profile signals to inlining, cache locality, algorithmic complexity, SIMD, and logging overhead patterns.

faq.question: Does it support production observability?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Prometheus, pprof, continuous profiling, alerting, and regression detection guidance.

faq.question: Is every suggested optimization safe?
faq.answer: No. The skill asks users to benchmark each change and avoid unsafe or experimental techniques unless the evidence justifies them.
